options.B: Because most maternal deaths from bleeding happen shortly after delivery
options.C: Because the mother's blood pressure always drops to zero
options.D: Because the baby cries continuously during the first few hours

explanation: Postpartum hemorrhage is most likely to occur immediately after the placenta is delivered, making early observation essential. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T44#GNS214_U1_T44_h4)

question: Why do healthcare teams sometimes clamp chest tubes for a short time after giving an intrapleural drug?

options.A: To stop the patient from coughing during the procedure
options.B: To keep the medication in contact with the pleural surfaces
options.C: To measure the exact hourly urine output of the patient
options.D: To prevent air from rushing into the sterile chest cavity

explanation: You've got it! Clamping keeps the drug inside long enough to do its job—like irritating the lining for a pleurodesis—instead of draining right out.

question: Why is asking about family and home life so important when assessing a patient with a skin rash?

options.A: It replaces the need for a physical skin examination
options.B: It helps identify if other household members share the same contact infection
options.C: It determines the exact antibiotic resistance profile of the organism
options.D: It proves whether the patient has a genetic predisposition to eczema

explanation: Contact infections love to bounce around families! Checking if others at home are scratching stops the vicious cycle of reinfection.

question: Which sign strongly suggests internal bleeding in a patient on blood thinners?

options.A: Complaints of severe itching on the arms and legs
options.B: A sudden rise in the patient's body temperature
options.C: An increase in urine output over twenty-four hours
options.D: The presence of dark, tarry stools in the bedpan

explanation: Dark, tarry stools are a classic warning sign of bleeding in the stomach or intestines. Spotting this early saves lives!

question: A patient scheduled for a procedure with mild sedation asks for a glass of water an hour beforehand. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Explain that fasting guidelines must be followed to prevent aspiration during sedation.
options.B: Ignore the question because fluid intake does not affect anesthesia safety.
options.C: Tell the patient to drink plenty of fluids to stay hydrated before the test.
options.D: Allow the patient to drink a small cup of water since it is just a liquid.

explanation: Fasting (NPO) keeps the stomach empty so the patient doesn't accidentally choke or inhale stomach contents while sedated. Safety first!

question: A toddler with a throat infection starts making a harsh, high-pitched breathing sound (stridor) and flaring their nose. What should you do right away?

options.A: Encourage the child to eat a large solid meal
options.B: Notify the healthcare provider and prepare for airway support
options.C: Discharge the child home with instructions to rest
options.D: Apply a tight nasal pack to stop the secretions

explanation: Great clinical judgment! Stridor and nasal flaring mean the airway is struggling or narrowing. Call the doctor immediately and get ready to help the child breathe.

question: How does ionization affect a drug's movement through the body?

options.A: Charged molecules have a harder time crossing cell membranes
options.B: Ionization has no effect on how medicine moves
options.C: Ionization stops the drug from ever entering the blood
options.D: Charged molecules move much faster through fat layers

explanation: Cell membranes don't like charged particles. So, if a drug is ionized, it tends to get stuck wherever it currently is instead of crossing over easily.

question: What was a major headache with early psychiatric classification systems?

options.A: Governments refused to fund any mental health research
options.B: They focused exclusively on genetic markers
options.C: Too many laboratory tests were required for admission
options.D: Inconsistencies between hospitals caused clinical confusion

explanation: Back in the day, different hospitals used totally different terms. This made sharing notes or comparing treatments a real struggle!

question: When does bereavement support typically begin and end in a hospice program?

options.A: It begins only after one full year has passed
options.B: It continues for months after the patient passes away
options.C: It only occurs during the final week of the patient's life
options.D: It stops immediately the moment the patient dies

explanation: Bereavement care is an ongoing service that supports grieving family members for many months following their loss. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T14#GNS324_U5_T14_h8)

question: What is the main difference between drug tolerance and psychological addiction?

options.A: Tolerance happens only in children; addiction happens in adults
options.B: Addiction is caused by paracetamol, tolerance by morphine
options.C: Tolerance means the drug stops working for any condition
options.D: Tolerance is a normal body adjustment needing higher doses, while addiction involves compulsive craving

explanation: Well explained! Tolerance just means your body gets used to a drug over time so you need a bit more for the same effect. Addiction is a complex behavioral drive to use drugs compulsively.

question: What does a simple frequency distribution table show us?

options.A: A map of hospital departments
options.B: The exact daily schedule of clinical staff
options.C: The financial budget of a hospital ward
options.D: How often specific values or categories occur

explanation: A frequency table simply counts and shows how many times a particular observation or response pops up in your data.

question: When a woman is diagnosed with cervical cancer, which two cell types are most commonly involved?

options.A: Sarcoma and transitional cell carcinoma
options.B: Melanoma and small cell carcinoma
options.C: Squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma
options.D: Lymphoma and clear cell carcinoma

explanation: You've got this! Squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma make up the vast majority of cervical cancers. They develop from the two main types of cells found on the cervix.

question: Which nurse is usually on the frontline tracking daily infections on the hospital wards?

options.A: The head pharmacist on duty
options.B: The director of human resources
options.C: The hospital chief executive
options.D: The infection control nurse

explanation: Correct! Infection control nurses spend their days right on the wards watching out for germs and teaching staff how to stay safe.

question: What does it mean when a Drug Revolving Fund is described as 'ring-fenced'?

options.A: The pharmacy door must be locked with a special metal ring
options.B: Drugs are arranged in circular shelves inside the store
options.C: Profits are shared equally among all clinical department heads
options.D: Money from drug sales is kept separate and used only to buy more drugs

explanation: Ring-fencing is like putting a protective fence around the money. It ensures drug funds aren't mistakenly used to pay for other hospital bills!

question: Which newborn scalp swelling is known for crossing right across the cranial suture lines?

options.A: Subgaleal hemorrhage
options.B: Cephalhematoma
options.C: Caput succedaneum
options.D: Subdural hematoma

explanation: Correct! Caput is just fluid under the scalp skin, so it easily crosses over the suture lines. Think of it like a soft, spongy cushion.

question: Which type of stretcher splits into two halves so you can slide it under a patient without rolling them?

options.A: Scoop stretcher
options.B: Basket stretcher
options.C: Canvas folding stretcher
options.D: Rigid spine board

explanation: Spot on! A scoop stretcher splits lengthwise, making it super helpful when you want to avoid rolling a fragile patient.

question: A patient cannot shrug their right shoulder or turn their head properly. Which nerve might be damaged?

options.A: Accessory nerve
options.B: Abducens nerve
options.C: Oculomotor nerve
options.D: Trochlear nerve

explanation: That's correct! The accessory nerve (CN XI) powers the neck and shoulder muscles we use to turn our head and lift our shoulders.

question: Why are supportive national policies so important for keeping reproductive health services running?

options.A: They secure long-term government funding and legal protection for healthcare programs
options.B: They allow individual hospitals to ignore international health standards
options.C: They prevent community members from asking questions about medical care
options.D: They ensure that healthcare providers never have to undergo professional training

explanation: National policies give healthcare programs the legal backing and steady funds they need to survive even when government leaders change. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h8)

question: Where is the majority of the fluid in your body actually stored?

options.A: Inside the body cells
options.B: Within the lymphatic channels
options.C: Inside the blood vessels
options.D: Surrounding the tissue cells

explanation: Great job! Most of our body water is kept safely tucked away right inside our cells (intracellular fluid). Think of it as the main water reservoir of the body!

question: For how many months should an infant be exclusively breastfed, according to health guidelines?

options.A: First twelve months
options.B: First nine months
options.C: First three months
options.D: First six months

explanation: Spot on! Exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months gives a baby all the water and nourishment they need—no extra water or food required yet!

question: An experienced nurse makes a genuine mistake because a broken shift schedule left them completely exhausted. How should the manager respond?

options.A: Suspend the nurse without pay to set an example for other staff members
options.B: Support the nurse while fixing the underlying shift scheduling process
options.C: Fire the nurse immediately for failing to maintain personal alertness
options.D: Report the nurse to the national licensing board for professional misconduct

explanation: You got it! When a flawed system causes human error, the smart move is to fix the system and support the worker, not dish out harsh punishment.

question: Why is postpartum hemorrhage a huge risk after a mother delivers twins?

options.A: The overstretched uterus contracts poorly after birth.
options.B: The placenta is always retained inside the fallopian tubes.
options.C: The mother has too much iron in her bloodstream.
options.D: Blood clotting factors completely disappear during labor.

explanation: Brilliant reasoning! Carrying multiples stretches the uterine muscles a lot. Afterward, it sometimes struggles to clamp back down firmly (we call this uterine atony), making bleeding a major risk to watch for.

question: What is a common way survivors of gender-based violence initially present in a clinic?

options.A: By demanding a police officer upon walking through the door
options.B: With vague, chronic complaints and unexplained physical symptoms
options.C: By immediately handing the nurse a written confession of abuse
options.D: With completely normal physical and mental health screenings

explanation: Fear and stigma often prevent immediate disclosure, leading survivors to seek care for headaches, body pain, or anxiety instead. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T12#GNS312_U4_T12_h3)

question: How does an infant acquire natural passive immunity from their mother?

options.A: Through receiving routine childhood routine immunizations
options.B: By producing antibodies after surviving a childhood illness
options.C: By inheriting active immune memory cells during conception
options.D: Through the transfer of maternal antibodies via breast milk

explanation: Maternal antibodies pass to the baby across the placenta and through breast milk, giving the newborn temporary protection against common infections. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h2)

question: What is the main job of the ureters in our body?

options.A: Filter waste products out of the blood
options.B: Concentrate electrolytes in the renal pelvis
options.C: Store urine until it is ready for excretion
options.D: Transport urine from the kidneys to the bladder

explanation: You've got this! Think of the ureters as plumbing pipes that carry urine from the kidneys down into the bladder.

question: What is the primary benefit of establishing a coordinated referral pathway for GBV survivors?

options.A: It prevents the survivor from having to repeat their traumatic story to every new agency
options.B: It guarantees that the perpetrator will receive a life prison sentence
options.C: It eliminates the need for nurses to document physical injuries
options.D: It automatically lowers the hospital's electricity and water bills

explanation: Seamless coordination reduces secondary trauma by sparing survivors from retelling painful details at every step. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T12#GNS312_U4_T12_h7)

question: You find an abandoned elderly woman in a village with no food or medical care. What is the best way to coordinate her care?

options.A: Connect her with local social welfare agencies and senior support programs
options.B: Tell her neighbors to handle it completely on their own
options.C: Wait until the federal health budget is reviewed next year
options.D: Admit her to the maternity ward for routine antenatal checks

explanation: You're thinking like a true nurse! Your role includes acting as a bridge, linking vulnerable patients directly to the social services and agencies equipped to help them long-term.

question: What type of institution served as the primary sanctuary for healing during the early medieval period?

options.A: Monasteries and convents
options.B: Private community pharmacies
options.C: University teaching clinics
options.D: Government public health offices

explanation: Religious institutions like monasteries and convents housed the earliest organized healthcare and nursing services. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h2)

question: Which physical sign might make a nurse suspect that an outpatient has anemia?

options.A: Swollen finger joints
options.B: Yellowing of the teeth
options.C: Pale conjunctiva
options.D: Excessive hair growth

explanation: You're doing great! Checking the inner eyelids (conjunctiva) for paleness is a quick way to spot low red blood cells or iron deficiency.

question: Why do we need to clearly identify our research problem before jumping into the study?

options.A: It guarantees the hospital will approve the project
options.B: It gives the entire study clear direction and focus
options.C: It prevents patients from asking questions
options.D: It removes the need for a literature review

explanation: Think of the problem statement as your map. When you know exactly what you are looking into, you won't wander around aimlessly while trying to collect your data.

question: Why do clinical trials sometimes miss some side effects before a drug is finally approved?

options.A: Regulatory agencies forbid companies from testing long-term effects
options.B: They involve too few patients and last for a limited time
options.C: Researchers deliberately hide minor side effect data from the public
options.D: Participants in clinical trials never take the correct drug dosage

explanation: Great thinking! Clinical trials only test a small group of people for a short while. Rare or long-term side effects often only show up later when millions of everyday people start taking the drug.

question: What is the primary focus of microbiology?

options.A: The chemical composition of human blood
options.B: The electrical signals of the nervous system
options.C: The study of microscopic living organisms
options.D: The physical structure of human bones

explanation: Microbiology specifically investigates organisms too small to be seen clearly with the naked eye. [learn more](GST114_U1_T1#GST114_U1_T1_h1)

question: What is the usual waiting time between taking mifepristone and taking misoprostol?

options.A: 5 to 7 days
options.B: 2 weeks
options.C: 24 to 48 hours
options.D: 1 to 2 hours

explanation: Spot on! Patients usually wait 24 to 48 hours after swallowing the mifepristone tablet before taking the misoprostol.

question: Which blood test result is a classic warning sign of severe internal poisoning from swallowed toxins?

options.A: An elevated platelet level
options.B: A high white blood cell count
options.C: A low serum sodium level
options.D: An increased anion gap

explanation: An increased anion gap tells you there is a buildup of hidden, dangerous acids circulating in the patient's blood.

question: In drug storage and inventory, what does the acronym FEFO mean?

options.A: First Expire, First Out
options.B: Facility Examined, Fully Opened
options.C: First Entered, Final Out
options.D: Fast Effect, Fast Observation

explanation: FEFO is a great habit! Use the drugs that will expire the earliest before you touch the newer shipments.

question: What is the correct management advice for a mother who develops mastitis in one breast?

options.A: Restrict all fluid intake to prevent the infection from spreading
options.B: Continue breastfeeding frequently to keep the milk draining out
options.C: Apply ice packs to freeze the infected milk inside the milk ducts
options.D: Stop feeding from the affected side completely until the pain stops

explanation: Frequent milk removal is vital in treating mastitis because letting milk pool in the breast makes the infection worse. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h6)

question: What can happen if the pelvic ligaments and fascia become weak?

options.A: Blood flow to the lower limbs is cut off
options.B: The thigh bones become unstable in the socket
options.C: Pelvic organs can descend or prolapse
options.D: Abdominal muscles stop contracting properly

explanation: Spot on. Without strong support from ligaments and fascia, gravity pulls the pelvic organs downward.

question: A patient says they want to stop eating all carbs immediately to lose weight fast. As their nurse, what is your best response?

options.A: Ignore their plan and give them a rigid calorie chart
options.B: Encourage them to double their water intake instead
options.C: Help them set smaller, realistic goals for gradual change
options.D: Tell them to stop eating completely for three days

explanation: Brilliant! Slow, steady lifestyle changes stick around much longer than sudden, painful restrictions. Guide them step by step.

question: What legal idea allows you to treat an unconscious trauma patient without their verbal permission?

options.A: Implied consent
options.B: Professional mandate
options.C: Expressed authority
options.D: Informed refusal

explanation: The law assumes that if an unconscious person could speak, they would definitely want you to save their life!

question: How does naloxone work to reverse an opioid overdose?

options.A: By speeding up renal excretion of the drug through urination
options.B: By binding directly to the free poison molecules in the stomach
options.C: By competing for and blocking opioid receptor sites
options.D: By stimulating the liver to break down the circulating toxin

explanation: Naloxone acts like a key that bumps the opioid off its lock (the receptor). By blocking those sites, it quickly wakes the patient up and helps them breathe again.

question: When food prices shoot up due to inflation, how do many families change what they eat?

options.A: They grow all their missing food requirements in backyard container gardens
options.B: They substitute nutrient-dense foods with cheaper, calorie-dense refined carbohydrates
options.C: They automatically increase their daily intake of fresh fruits and lean meats
options.D: They stop eating entirely until government food subsidies arrive in the mail

explanation: When money gets tight, families swap out expensive veggies and proteins for cheaper filler foods that fill the belly but lack vitamins.

question: What is the name of the tough outer covering that wraps around an entire peripheral nerve?

options.A: Meninges
options.B: Epineurium
options.C: Endoneurium
options.D: Perineurium

explanation: That's correct! The epineurium is the strong outer coat that shields the nerve from everyday bumps and wear-and-tear.

question: How does heavy data scatter (noise) inside your groups affect your final t-score?

options.A: It makes the t-statistic smaller
options.B: It makes the t-statistic larger
options.C: It has no effect on the t-statistic
options.D: It turns the t-statistic into a negative decimal

explanation: Since variability sits at the bottom (denominator) of the math formula, a bigger scatter makes your final t-score shrink.

question: What is the main goal of conducting a community diagnosis?

options.A: To enforce federal health laws and penalize local market vendors
options.B: To identify local health problems and community assets systematically
options.C: To diagnose individual patients visiting the tertiary hospital ward
options.D: To calculate the exact hospital budget required for surgery units

explanation: Instead of looking at one patient, a community diagnosis looks at the whole town to find out what health challenges they face and what resources they already have.

question: How do nurses protect a patient's limb from clots and tissue damage when an arterial catheter is in place?

options.A: By keeping the patient's blood pressure as low as surgically possible
options.B: By soaking the entire limb in warm water every thirty minutes
options.C: By regularly injecting large air bubbles into the arterial tubing
options.D: By monitoring distal perfusion and maintaining a continuous flush system

explanation: Brilliant! Keeping the flush system running smoothly stops clots from forming, and checking the fingers or toes often ensures blood is flowing nicely.

question: Which Nigerian body is in charge of registering nurses and looking after our professional discipline?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Health
options.B: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.C: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.D: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration

explanation: Spot on! The NMCN is our very own guardian angel body set up by law to guide nursing training and practice right here in Nigeria.

question: Why is it so helpful to involve family members when giving diet counseling to a patient?

options.A: It prevents the patient from ever eating outside the home
options.B: Family members pay all the hospital medical bills
options.C: Family members usually prepare the household meals and manage food purchases
options.D: Family members are legally required to taste all hospital food first

explanation: Since family members are usually the ones cooking at home, bringing them into the conversation ensures the new diet is actually doable for the household!

question: What is meant by 'capacity building' in community health projects?

options.A: Increasing the salary of foreign NGO directors
options.B: Purchasing more vehicles for administrative travel
options.C: Building larger physical warehouses for medical drugs
options.D: Training local community members to sustain initiatives

explanation: Exactly! Capacity building is about teaching locals the skills they need to keep running their own health programs successfully. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h6)

question: What is the main goal of a receptor antagonist antidote?

options.A: To coat the intestinal lining and prevent food digestion
options.B: To occupy the same receptor sites and block the toxin from attaching
options.C: To destroy the toxin molecule directly inside the stomach
options.D: To stimulate the liver to store extra glucose for energy

explanation: An antagonist gets to the parking spot (receptor) first and refuses to leave, blocking the toxin from parking there and causing trouble!

question: Which fracture type involves the broken bone piercing through the skin?

options.A: Closed fracture
options.B: Greenstick fracture
options.C: Transverse fracture
options.D: Open fracture

explanation: An open or compound fracture breaks through the skin surface, carrying a high risk of bacterial contamination and infection. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T10#GNS222_U1_T10_h2)

question: What is the main job of the pulmonary circulation?

options.A: To filter waste products out of the kidneys
options.B: To transport blood between the heart and lungs
options.C: To absorb nutrients from digested food
options.D: To deliver oxygen directly to the brain

explanation: You got this! Pulmonary circulation simply moves blood between your heart and lungs so your red blood cells can drop off carbon dioxide and pick up fresh oxygen.

question: Which physical sign strongly points to dehydration in a patient with severe vomiting and diarrhea?

options.A: Swelling in both lower legs and ankles
options.B: Flushed, warm skin with heavy sweating
options.C: A slow, bounding pulse and high blood pressure
options.D: Poor skin turgor and dry mucous membranes

explanation: Spot on! When fluid drains out from vomiting and diarrhea, the mouth gets dry and the skin loses its snap (turgor). Excellent clinical eye!

question: A patient arrives with a massive pulmonary embolism. What is happening in their body?

options.A: Blood flow through the pulmonary arteries is blocked, impairing oxygenation
options.B: The liver has stopped producing clotting factors, causing widespread bleeding
options.C: An infection in the urinary tract has spread into the spinal fluid
options.D: Gastric acid is leaking directly into the peritoneal cavity through an ulcer

explanation: A pulmonary embolism is a blocked blood vessel in the lungs. Because the blockage is there, blood can't pick up fresh oxygen to circulate.

question: What is the main goal of birth preparedness and complication readiness (BPCR) during antenatal care?

options.A: To train family members to deliver the baby at home safely
options.B: To prevent dangerous delays in reaching emergency obstetric care
options.C: To remove the financial cost of hospital supplies completely
options.D: To guarantee that the baby is born on the exact estimated date

explanation: BPCR is all about planning ahead (transport, funds, blood donors) so that if an emergency strikes, the mother doesn't lose precious time.

question: What should you do immediately if your patient starts coughing violently and turning blue while you are passing a tube?

options.A: Ask the patient to take a deep breath and swallow
options.B: Push the tube down faster to clear the way
options.C: Stop pushing and pull the tube right back out
options.D: Inject water to wash it down

explanation: Coughing and turning blue (cyanosis) means the tube has mistakenly slipped into the windpipe instead of the food pipe. Pull it back out immediately and let them catch their breath!

question: Which of these is NOT a typical complication linked to habitual hot bath practices?

options.A: Accidental scalding or thermal burns of vulvar tissues
options.B: Delayed healing of fresh postpartum perineal wounds
options.C: Permanent cessation of natural ovarian hormone production
options.D: Recurrent vaginal infections due to microbiome disruption

explanation: While hot baths can cause burns or infections, they don't shut down your ovaries! You're doing great learning what hot water can and cannot do to the body.

question: Which special cells in your stomach lining pump out hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor?

options.A: Chief cells
options.B: G cells
options.C: Mucous cells
options.D: Parietal cells

explanation: You've got it. Parietal cells are the stomach's acid factories, producing both the hydrochloric acid needed for digestion and intrinsic factor to help absorb vitamin B12.

question: What is the main difference between short-acting and long-acting beta-2 agonists?

options.A: Short-acting drugs are used for COPD, while long-acting drugs are only for asthma
options.B: Short-acting drugs are taken as pills, while long-acting drugs can only be injected
options.C: Short-acting drugs give quick relief during attacks, while long-acting drugs provide daily maintenance
options.D: Short-acting drugs reduce inflammation, while long-acting drugs only relax muscles

explanation: Short-acting drugs are your quick-fix rescue inhalers for sudden tightness, while long-acting drugs work quietly in the background all day to keep airways open.

question: You are managing a patient with acute PPH. Which of these actions is completely WRONG and dangerous?

options.A: Checking vital signs every 5 to 15 minutes
options.B: Instructing the patient to walk around to encourage drainage
options.C: Calling for help from the multidisciplinary team right away
options.D: Setting up large-bore IV lines for fluid replacement

explanation: Never let a bleeding, shock-prone patient walk around! That can instantly cause her blood pressure to bottom out and lead to a collapse. Strict bed rest is a must.

question: Which everyday task puts women in displacement camps at high risk of physical attack?

options.A: Receiving dry food rations directly from aid workers
options.B: Attending mandatory community health education workshops
options.C: Walking long distances alone to collect firewood and water
options.D: Participating in organized camp leadership meetings during the day

explanation: Going out to fetch water or firewood means walking through lonely, unlit areas far from help. It's a huge safety hazard for women in camps.

question: Why shouldn't you rush or speed too much when transporting an accident victim?

options.A: Vehicles consume too much fuel when driven too fast
options.B: Rushing can compromise the airway or worsen existing injuries
options.C: Hospitals prefer patients to arrive slowly for administrative reasons
options.D: Rescuers get too tired to document the incident properly

explanation: Spot on! Moving too fast without control can cause dropped stretchers or mess up breathing tubes. Smooth and steady wins the race in emergency care.

question: What is the medical term for the natural loss of muscle mass and strength as people age?

options.A: The rapid calcification of heart valves in older adults
options.B: The abnormal softening of bones due to vitamin deficiency
options.C: The sudden inflammation of fluid-filled joint sacs
options.D: The progressive loss of skeletal muscle mass and function

explanation: That's sarcopenia! It's just the natural decrease in muscle size and strength that happens as our bodies age.

question: Why must nurses carefully separate the concepts of sex and gender during patient assessments?

options.A: To change hospital administrative policies
options.B: To diagnose chromosomal disorders more cheaply
options.C: To avoid making false clinical assumptions about a patient based only on their anatomy
options.D: To ensure laboratory tests run faster

explanation: Brilliant! Knowing the difference stops us from stereotyping patients and helps us give safe, individualized care.

question: What are the core checks to perform during a neurovascular assessment of a limb in traction?

options.A: Joint range, breath sounds, and pulses
options.B: Pain scale, pin length, and skin turgor
options.C: Circulation, motion, and sensation
options.D: Temperature, weight, and muscle tone

explanation: You nailed it! Always remember the ABCs of neurovascular checks: checking if blood is flowing (circulation), if they can move (motion), and if they can feel (sensation).

question: What is a sample in a research study?

options.A: A small subset of people chosen to represent a larger population
options.B: A chemical substance tested in a laboratory beaker
options.C: The final written report published in a journal
options.D: The budget allocated for purchasing hospital supplies

explanation: Researchers study a sample because it is usually impossible to measure every single person in a target population. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h4)

question: A community health nurse wants to start a nutrition program in a rural village. What is the best first step following PHC philosophy?

options.A: Build a modern multi-story hospital in the center of the village
options.B: Consult with local community leaders and residents to identify their actual nutritional priorities
options.C: Import expensive foreign dietary supplements and distribute them immediately
options.D: Report the villagers to local authorities for poor feeding habits

explanation: You got it! Community participation always starts by listening to the people first and letting them help identify their own needs and solutions.

question: A patient on chemotherapy calls the clinic saying their temperature is 38.5°C. What should you tell them to do?

options.A: Drink plenty of cold fluids and monitor the temperature for another day.
options.B: Apply a cool damp cloth to the forehead to bring down the fever.
options.C: Take a dose of paracetamol and rest in bed until tomorrow morning.
options.D: Come to the hospital immediately for a medical evaluation and blood work.

explanation: Fever in a chemo patient is an emergency because their immune system is low. Quick action can save a life!

question: Which part of the brain acts as the master control center to start the menstrual cycle?

options.A: The adrenal gland
options.B: The thyroid gland
options.C: The pituitary gland
options.D: The hypothalamus

explanation: Think of the hypothalamus as the head office in the brain—it sends the very first signal (GnRH) to kick off the cycle!

question: Why do we keep the head of the bed slightly elevated for a patient with increased intracranial pressure from encephalitis?

options.A: To make sure the patient can see people walking into the room
options.B: To make swallowing oral pills easier
options.C: To help blood drain smoothly from the head and lower the pressure
options.D: To stop spit from going down the wrong pipe

explanation: Raising the bed to about 30 degrees uses gravity to help blood flow down smoothly through the jugular veins, keeping pressure inside the skull under control.

question: What is the very first link in the chain of infection?

options.A: Susceptible host
options.B: Portal of entry
options.C: Mode of transmission
options.D: Causative agent

explanation: Think of the causative agent as the starting point—it's the actual germ (like bacteria or a virus) that causes the disease!

question: Why do nurses need to provide individualized care instead of treating every pregnant woman the exact same way?

options.A: It ensures that all pregnant women take the exact same supplements
options.B: Medical doctors refuse to see patients who follow standard routines
options.C: Standard hospital guidelines are illegal to use in public clinics
options.D: Every woman has unique social, cultural, and physiological needs

explanation: No two mothers are alike! Factoring in her background, culture, and unique body helps you give care that truly fits her life.

question: Why do we carry an antiseptic solution like chlorhexidine in the infection prevention pack?

options.A: To act as an energy drink for tired mothers in labor
options.B: To serve as a nice jelly for easing dryness
options.C: To clean and prep the skin before exams or procedures
options.D: To quickly wipe down and clean rusty metal scissors

explanation: Antiseptic solutions lower the number of germs on the skin, which protects the mother and baby from nasty infections during delivery.

question: What should be prepared ahead of time in case an emergency happens during a home birth?

options.A: Traditional dancing costumes for visitors
options.B: Transport arrangements and emergency contact numbers
options.C: Extra cooking utensils for the family
options.D: A formal letter of apology to the hospital

explanation: Having transport and contacts ready prevents deadly delays when seconds count during an unexpected crisis. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T9#GNS225_U3_T9_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal local reaction to a topical drug?

options.A: Contact dermatitis at the site
options.B: Local burning or stinging
options.C: Anaphylactic shock originating in the lungs
options.D: Pruritus and skin redness

explanation: Anaphylactic shock is a serious whole-body allergic emergency, whereas local reactions only happen right where you applied the cream.

question: What is the main goal of Human Resource Management (HRM) in a hospital?

options.A: Determining the hospital financial budget for the year
options.B: Repairing and maintaining hospital medical equipment
options.C: Managing staff from recruitment to retirement
options.D: Purchasing drugs and medical supplies for the pharmacy

explanation: Think of HR as the backbone for the people side of healthcare! HRM takes care of staff members right from when they apply for a job all the way to when they retire.

question: How does poor lighting contribute to home accidents?

options.A: It lowers the body temperature of elderly residents
options.B: it attracts insects that carry harmful infections
options.C: It hides obstacles and changes in floor levels
options.D: It causes sudden dizziness and fainting spells

explanation: When rooms or hallways are dim, people cannot clearly see rugs, electrical cords, or steps, making them trip. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h2)

question: What is the term for weak, lazy uterine contractions that fail to open the cervix?

options.A: Occiput posterior
options.B: Cephalopelvic disproportion
options.C: Uterine inertia
options.D: Uterine hyperstimulation

explanation: Spot on! 'Inertia' means lack of movement or energy. The uterus is simply too tired or weak to push the process along.

question: Which item must always be placed within a patient's easy reach before you leave the room after making their bed?

options.A: The room key and visitor pass
options.B: The spare pillowcase stack
options.C: The patient call light
options.D: The clinical chart and nursing clipboard

explanation: Correct! The call light is your patient's lifeline to ask for help. Keeping it close by prevents dangerous attempts to climb out of bed unassisted.

question: What is a main characteristic of primary health care?

options.A: It is delivered solely by medical specialists inside tertiary hospitals
options.B: It is restricted only to wealthy individuals with private health insurance
options.C: It provides universally accessible and affordable care to the community
options.D: It focuses exclusively on expensive surgical procedures in capital cities

explanation: Primary health care is designed to be universally accessible, affordable, and acceptable to all members of the community. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h6)

question: Why do water-soluble vitamins dissolve easily in our blood?

options.A: They are built from long chains of saturated fatty acids
options.B: They consist entirely of interlocking cholesterol rings
options.C: Their chemical structures contain many polar groups
options.D: They contain heavy mineral salt deposits

explanation: Like dissolves like! Polar parts of the vitamin love interacting with water, allowing them to travel smoothly through the bloodstream.

question: What is the main drawback of using a 24-hour dietary recall?

options.A: It requires expensive laboratory equipment
options.B: It relies heavily on the patient's memory
options.C: It measures blood chemistry instead of food
options.D: It takes months to complete and analyze

explanation: People easily forget what they ate yesterday, which can lead to a few blank spots in a 24-hour recall!

question: Why do sutures need to be taken out instead of left inside the body permanently?

options.A: Skin cells will permanently grow over the thread and trap it in bone.
options.B: Non-absorbable threads act as foreign objects that can trigger infection.
options.C: The body will naturally dissolve all types of suture material within a week.
options.D: Permanent synthetic threads interfere with normal skin sensation forever.

explanation: Non-absorbable materials do not break down inside the body and will cause chronic irritation or abscess formation if left indefinitely. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h1)

question: You are preparing a recovery bed for a patient coming back from theatre. Which item must you keep ready at the bedside?

options.A: An overhead exercise trapeze bar
options.B: Suction apparatus and emesis basin
options.C: Bedside dining tray and reading lamp
options.D: A heavy woolen floor rug and extra pillows

explanation: Great job! Patients waking up from anesthesia can easily choke on saliva or vomit, so having a suction machine and a basin nearby is a lifesaver.

question: Why are 'standing orders' so important in a rural maternity clinic?

options.A: They give midwives the power to perform major surgical operations independently
options.B: They provide legal authorization for midwives to give specific drugs without a doctor present
options.C: They replace the need for keeping patient health records and drug registers
options.D: They allow patients to purchase restricted medications over the counter without a prescription

explanation: Think of standing orders as your legal safety net—pre-approved protocols that let you step in with emergency treatment right away.

question: Why should you avoid giving rectal medications to a patient who has active rectal bleeding?

options.A: The patient will automatically develop an allergic reaction to the drug
options.B: The medication can worsen mucosal damage and might be washed away
options.C: The drug will bypass the liver entirely and cause immediate toxicity
options.D: The rectal sphincter will permanently lock shut and trap the medicine

explanation: Active bleeding or severe diarrhea stops the drug from being absorbed properly and can hurt the already irritated tissues.

question: How does your brain figure out which direction a sound is coming from?

options.A: By measuring how much earwax blocks the external auditory canal
options.B: By tracking the movement of the stapes bone against the oval window
options.C: By comparing the slight time and loudness differences between both ears
options.D: By analyzing the chemical balance of perilymph fluid in the cochlea

explanation: Because your ears are on opposite sides of your head, a sound hits the closer ear a split second faster and louder than the other. Your brain calculates this tiny difference to pinpoint the direction!

question: Why is smoking tobacco such a major risk factor for many types of cancer?

options.A: It introduces living cancer cells into the lungs
options.B: It blocks all major blood vessels
options.C: It contains harmful chemicals that damage cellular DNA
options.D: It stops red blood cells from forming

explanation: Tobacco smoke has active chemical carcinogens that mess up the genetic code inside healthy cells, triggering abnormal growth.

question: Which living condition makes the rapid spread of airborne respiratory infections much easier?

options.A: Overcrowded housing with poor ventilation
options.B: Living in a dry and dusty rural climate
options.C: Residing near a flowing freshwater river
options.D: Consuming food cooked over open firewood

explanation: Spot on! When people are packed tightly together with stale air, respiratory droplets pass easily from one person to the next.

question: A male patient with severe chest pain waited three days to visit the clinic because he felt he had to 'be strong' for his family. Which concept best explains this delay?

options.A: An innate genetic flaw in male chromosome pairing
options.B: Socially constructed gender roles influencing health-seeking behavior
options.C: A standard physiological reaction to low blood pressure
options.D: An intersex hormonal imbalance affecting pain receptors

explanation: You're doing great! Traditional masculine expectations to be stoic can sadly stop men from seeking quick medical attention.

question: How do corticosteroids stop swelling and inflammation in the body?

options.A: By blocking nerve impulses that transmit localized pain signals
options.B: By freezing cell membranes to prevent white blood cells from moving
options.C: By directly neutralizing circulating bacteria in the bloodstream
options.D: By altering DNA transcription to stop inflammatory chemical production

explanation: Steroids go right into cell nuclei to switch off the genes that create inflammatory chemicals. That's how they calm down swelling at the root!

question: Your rural clinic keeps losing vaccines because of erratic power supply. What is the best immediate response that uses local community resources?

options.A: Wait for the federal government to rebuild the entire national electrical grid
options.B: Partner with local market leaders to mobilize a solar backup or reliable cold box system
options.C: Close the clinic permanently and refer all children to hospitals in the capital city
options.D: Blame the local residents for failing to generate their own electricity

explanation: Brilliant problem-solving! Instead of waiting for distant solutions, tapping into local networks and leaders helps you find practical, community-driven fixes right away.
